issues.description: Console warning: 'Please ensure that the container has a non-static position, like relative, fixed, or absolute to ensure scroll offset is calculated correctly.' This indicates a scroll/position utility (likely react-scroll or a custom scroll hook) is being mounted on a statically-positioned container. Not visible to the user but indicates a layout/ref misconfiguration.
issues.element: Scroll container wrapper (likely wrapping the hero or page root)
issues.root_cause: A component using a scroll-offset library (e.g., react-scroll's Element or a custom useScrollOffset hook) is rendered inside a div without an explicit CSS position property set to 'relative', 'fixed', or 'absolute'. The default position is 'static', which causes the warning.

issues.description: page:mount event fires twice for step-1 (timestamps 1776404296929/934 and 1776404299367/369). This suggests StrictMode double-invocation or a component unmounting and remounting, potentially causing duplicate analytics events.
issues.element: Page mount event emitter in step-1 page component
issues.root_cause: React StrictMode in development intentionally double-invokes effects. If the analytics event is fired inside a useEffect without proper cleanup or deduplication, it will fire twice. In production this would not occur with StrictMode, but the double-mount could also indicate an actual remount (e.g., router re-rendering the component).

issues.description: Gold particle animation on dark navy canvas cannot be visually confirmed from a static screenshot. The expected behavior specifies particles animating, but a still image cannot verify motion. No canvas element or particle overlay is visibly distinct in the screenshot.
issues.root_cause: Cannot determine from static screenshot whether the canvas/WebGL particle system is running. The canvas may be present but invisible at z-index below content, or the animation may not have started. No JS errors reported, so it may be functioning correctly.

fixes.reason: Adds a non-static position to the root page container to resolve the scroll offset warning from the scroll utility library. Alternatively add 'relative' to the Tailwind className.
Guards the analytics event with a ref flag so it only fires once even in React StrictMode's double-invocation of effects, preventing duplicate page:mount events in analytics.
